Ntizo Listings Refresh
Ntizo · Listings refresh v2 /services and /providers · proposal with mock data · 6 Sep 2026
Why Services Providers Map Mobile States What it needs

v2 · what changed after your feedback

Take the boxes away

v1 kept the shape of a template: a tinted ground, every element in a bordered rounded box, a sidebar of checkboxes. v2 is a white page where the photographs do the work. Nothing is boxed; hairlines separate only what needs separating. Search lives in the header, filters are a light toolbar, and the grid uses the whole width.

Six decisions

  1. No boxes

    White page. A tile is a photograph with three lines of text under it. No border, no shadow, no tinted ground. This is how Airbnb, Etsy and Fresha list, and it is why they look expensive.

  2. Search in the header

    One pill in the middle of the header holds the service and the city. The pill nav goes; Serviços and Prestadores become two words on the right. The page starts with results.

  3. Categories as an icon strip

    Small icon over a small label, underlined when chosen, scrolling sideways. It reads as navigation, not as a row of buttons.

  4. Filters as a toolbar, not a sidebar

    Dropdown pills under the heading, the applied ones filled navy. The sidebar goes and the grid gets four tiles per row: 12 results above the fold.

  5. Businesses as rows, with a map

    Hairline rows with the photo, the logo, what they sell and what it costs. A map view for providers is drawn as phase two; it needs coordinates the data does not have yet.

  6. Mobile rebuilt

    A search pill, the icon strip, quick-filter chips, hairline list rows with a square photo, a floating Filtros / Ordenar control, and a real filter sheet.

The tile is a photograph and three lines. Name with the rating beside it, who and where, price with duration and place. Verified is the navy seal on the provider's name. No category chip on the photo: the strip above already says which category you are in, and in “Todos” the photo says it.

Applied filters are the filled pills. “Preço fixo” is on, so it is navy and carries its own ×. The others open a small panel with the options v1 had in the sidebar; nothing is lost, it just stops taking a quarter of the page.

Blue appears once, on the search button. Everything else is navy, ink, grey and the amber star.

Rows, not cards. A business needs more words than a service, so it gets width instead of a box. A hairline between rows is all the separation the eye needs.

The row shows what the business sells. Up to three services with prices sit inside the row. This is the one thing the current page cannot say, and it needs one addition to the read model.

Rating top right, price under it. The two numbers a reader weighs share a column. The circle chevron is the row's only affordance; the whole row is the link.

Search pill, then the icon strip, then quick filters. The three most common narrowings (fixed price, at home, verified) are one tap on a chip. Everything else is in the sheet, which ends with a button that says how many results it will show.

List rows with a square photo, four on a screen, no boxes. The whole row is the tap target.

One floating control instead of a full-width bar: Filtros and Ordenar on services, Filtros and Mapa on providers. It stays at the thumb and covers nothing important.

Honest about the data

What this needs that the pages do not have today

Provider rows: up to three services with name and price. One array on the public provider read model, capped server-side. Everything else on both list pages renders from fields that already exist.

Map view: provider coordinates. Providers carry a city and a district, not a point. Geocoding the address at save time, or asking for a pin in provider settings, is its own piece of work; the map is phase two.

Header search on browse pages. The shared header gains a variant with the search pill in the middle and text nav on the right. The landing page keeps its own hero search.

Figtree and navy. The brand manual's typeface and its navy #00244C. One font import and one token; the font change is site-wide.

Not proposed, because no data exists for it: next free slot, response time, “hired N times”. The “Hoje” quick filter on the phone is drawn to show where availability would go once the read model exists.
